findings.who: A filer who receives an installment payment in 2025 from a sale made in 2021 and did not sell anything in 2025.
findings.why_no: They read 'In 2025, did you ... sell' as requiring a 2025 sale, and 'comes in a year after the year of the sale' as a future payment rather than a 2025 payment from an older sale.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 6, Installment Sales: 'Also, use Form 6252 to report any payment received in 2025 from a sale made in an earlier year that you reported on the installment method.'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Did you receive in 2025 any payment from a sale you made in 2025 or an earlier year, or will you receive a payment after 2025 from a 2025 sale?'

findings.who: A married filer filing jointly whose spouse alone received an installment payment in 2025 from a sale the spouse made in 2021.
findings.why_no: The first sentence says 'you (or, on a joint return, your spouse),' but the installment-payment sentence says only 'anything you sold'; read literally, the spouse's sale is not covered.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 6, Installment Sales: 'Also, use Form 6252 to report any payment received in 2025 from a sale made in an earlier year that you reported on the installment method.'
findings.fix: Add 'you or your spouse' to the installment-payment clause.

findings.who: A filer whose business property or investment real estate held more than one year for profit was condemned in 2025 and converted to cash, with no sale or trade by the filer.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether they sold or traded; a condemnation is an involuntary conversion, and the gated question also asks business/rental/mineral or non-investment property, so investment real estate is excluded.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Other Forms You May Have To File: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... The involuntary conversion (other than from casualty or theft) of property used in a trade or business and capital assets held more than 1 year for business or profit.'
findings.fix: Broaden the gate and the Form 4797 question to include involuntary conversions of business property and capital assets held more than one year for business or profit.

findings.who: A filer who sold section 1244 small business stock at an ordinary loss, or whose section 1244 stock became worthless, or who had a section 1242 small business investment company stock loss.
findings.why_no: They see stock as an investment, not 'real estate or business property,' so they answer no; the gate never reaches the Form 4797 refusal.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Other Forms You May Have To File: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... Ordinary loss on the sale, exchange, or worthlessness of small business investment company (section 1242) stock' and 'small business (section 1244) stock.'
findings.fix: Ask broadly about any sale, exchange, or worthlessness reportable on Form 4797, including sections 1242 and 1244 stock, instead of limiting the gate to real estate or business property.

findings.who: A trader who made a mark-to-market election and sold securities or commodities held in connection with that trading business in 2025.
findings.why_no: The help lists equipment, a vehicle, and a building, so the filer reads 'business property' as tangible business assets and treats exchange-traded securities as investments.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Other Forms You May Have To File: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... Ordinary gain or loss on securities or commodities held in connection with your trading business, if you previously made a mark-to-market election.'
findings.fix: Add a specific gate for securities or commodities held in a trading business with a mark-to-market election, or ask broadly about Form 4797 dispositions.

findings.who: A filer who exchanged vacant investment real estate for other real estate in a like-kind exchange and did not live on it or rent it out.
findings.why_no: The help says real estate includes a home lived in and an oil, gas, or mineral interest, so the filer reads the list as the relevant kinds of real estate and answers no because the land was neither.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Other Forms You May Have To File: 'Use Form 8824 to report like-kind exchanges. A like-kind exchange occurs when you exchange business or investment property for property of a like kind.'
findings.fix: Say that real estate includes any real property, such as vacant land or investment real estate, not just a home or mineral interest.

findings.who: A gig worker who sold a car used for rideshare or delivery but did not treat the activity as a business.
findings.why_no: They read 'business property' as requiring a formal business, despite the help mentioning a vehicle used in a business.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 1, Other Forms You May Have To File: 'Use Form 4797 to report ... Depreciable and amortizable tangible property used in your trade or business.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the vehicle was used for any business, including gig work, and state that a formal business entity is not required.
